artifacts.title: Functionally Constrained Algorithm Solves Convex Simple Bilevel Problems
A Near-Optimal Algorithm for Convex Simple Bilevel Optimization under Weak Assumptions
On Finding Small Hyper-Gradients in Bilevel Optimization: Hardness Results and Improved Analysis

public_problem: Design a target-neutral first-order bilevel optimization procedure for the supplied oracle family. Return one point for each of four fixed seeds within 4,000 oracle calls. The hidden evaluator checks lower-level validity, upper-level progress, finite outputs and seed reproducibility. You may use only the frozen pre-cutoff evidence in this capsule and the declared Python interface. Both upper and lower objectives may be nonconvex.

assumptions: Both objectives are differentiable with Lipschitz gradients on a bounded domain.
The lower objective has a nonempty solution set, but convexity is not assumed.
The algorithm receives first-order oracle access and a fixed oracle-call budget.

research_context.formal_problem: Given smooth nonconvex functions f and g, minimize f(z) over points that minimize g(z). A candidate returns one point per seed after a fixed number of first-order oracle calls. The evaluator separately measures upper descent residual and lower stationarity residual.

known_failures_and_conflicts.summary: Optimizing only the lower objective can converge to a lower stationary point with poor upper objective value.
Optimizing only the upper objective can violate the lower optimality requirement.

known_results.summary: Pre-cutoff methods for convex simple bilevel problems use weak solution concepts and functional constraints to avoid an unavailable exact lower optimum.
Pre-cutoff hardness results show that a small hyper-gradient alone is not a reliable universal target without additional structure.

research_context.research_question: How should a first-order method balance upper and lower objectives to reach a reproducible joint-stationary point when both objectives are nonconvex?
